page: Amazon Web Services m5ad.24xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based instance designed around high-density multithreaded compute and integrated high-speed local storage. Powered by first-generation AMD EPYC 7571 processors operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz, the instance supplies 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It integrates 384 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining the standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio characteristic of AWS general-purpose platforms. In addition to 20 Gbps of baseline networking capacity, the instance incorporates 3,600 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage. Hardware acceleration is limited to integrated cryptographic instruction sets, with no discrete GPU accelerators available.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture optimized for parallel execution rather than single-threaded responsiveness. Single-core tests, such as Geekbench single-core (725.0) and single-core stress-ng (590.99), place in the lower tier of cloud offerings, reflecting the IPC limits and lower clock speeds of the EPYC 7571 architecture. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression similarly show modest throughput. Conversely, highly parallelized tasks yield consistent mid-tier performance, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 47,316.06 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,199.0. Cryptographic performance is a distinct strength, reaching 77,626.79 in PassMark CPU encryption due to dedicated hardware instruction support. Cached memory bandwidth reaches 3,712.61 GB/sec, while uncached reads and writes sustain 181.6 GB/sec and 89.72 GB/sec, respectively.

The primary resource tradeoff centers on core density versus per-thread latency. While individual thread execution is relatively slow, the provision of 96 dedicated vCPUs, coupled with 3.6 TB of high-speed local NVMe scratch space, delivers high aggregate throughput per instance deployment. This makes the m5ad.24xlarge suitable for distributed cache systems, multi-threaded batch compilation, data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving environments that require rapid local disk access without demanding cutting-edge single-threaded IPC.
description: Amazon Web Services m5ad.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 96 vCPUs across 48 physical AMD EPYC 7571 cores at 2.2 GHz, 384 GB of DDR4 memory, and 3,600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the AWS Nitro System with 20 Gbps baseline networking, it maintains a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Benchmark data reveals modest single-thread performance, with low scores in single-core stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations. However, aggregate multithreaded metrics remain consistent, showing solid parallel throughput across PassMark CPU evaluations, Clang compilation, and static web serving benchmarks, alongside strong hardware-accelerated encryption throughput. The 3.6 TB bundled NVMe scratch space and high core count make this instance cost-effective for multi-threaded batch jobs, temporary database caching, distributed ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency web services where high parallel capacity takes precedence over single-core speed.
